public_rationale: There is no deadline. Reuters reports that Anthropic claimed adjusted profitability for the third quarter of 2026, which materially challenges the wording any kind of profitability. However, the retrieved report does not explain the adjustments. Treating that announcement as net profitability would substitute a different measure. No decisive event meeting the stated rule is established, so the forecast remains open.
limitations: A literal reading that accepts any company-described adjusted profit could produce a different result.
The lack of a qualifying event by October 28, 2026 is not evidence that profitability will never occur.
The reported profit comes from investor-meeting attendees rather than published reconciled quarterly accounts.

statement.excerpt: Yet the sheer fury of Anthropic’s customers only proves the fundamental weakness of Anthropic’s business model, and the impossibility of ever finding any kind of profitability.
statement.document_title: The Subprime AI Crisis Is Here

from_speaker: the fundamental weakness of Anthropic’s business model
the impossibility of ever finding any kind of profitability
our_interpretation: The checkable commitment is that Anthropic will never become profitable. Customer anger is offered as a reason, not an antecedent that must occur before the forecast applies.
The ordinary business reading is company-wide profitability after the costs of operating and maintaining the business.
A completed profitable quarter can contradict ever; I do not add a requirement for several profitable years.
Because any kind is broad, reconciled adjusted profitability must be considered. An undefined adjusted measure is insufficient to determine whether the business actually covers its recurring costs.
No accounting basis or deadline is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Anthropic permanently ceases operating, with sufficiently complete lifetime financial records showing that it never achieved company-wide profitability.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A completed reporting period establishes company-wide profitability on a disclosed basis that covers recurring business costs. A reconciled adjusted result may qualify; gross margin or a forecast alone does not.
